summary: Tsutomu Hatai worked in Indology and other fields. Attested in 1987, he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society.

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber (~1908–1912) and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University (1953). He held posts at Tokyo, Tohoku University (professor 1940–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Hokkaido University. He has served as a collaborative researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).
Tsyben Zhamtsarano was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Tunghai University and Harvard University. A longtime Harvard professor (1981–2010) and Harvard-Yenching Institute director (1996–2008), he later became Chair Professor of Humanities at Peking University (~2010).
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Tubten Nyendrak was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Shenphen Nangwa, and taught Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Palden Sherab and Ringu Tulku.
Tukaram Laddu specialized in Indology and linguistics. He completed studies at the University of Halle by 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Tulku Sherdor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, learning from Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Dodrupchen Monastery and under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche. He served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master who studied under Samten Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, among others. He founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery and taught numerous prominent figures.

Turrell V. Wylie was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who earned his B.A. at the University of Washington and studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He spent his career at the University of Washington, becoming professor in 1970.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Tyler Dewar is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Nitartha Institute (attested 2008, 2019). He studied under Acharya Tashi Wangchuk, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche.
Tyler G. Neill is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig by 2022 and held an attested post there in 2022.

Tzungkuen Wen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Queensland (2009). He lectured at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (2005) and headed the Counseling and Guidance Center at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
